objective: Independently test whether missing MPFR thread-local cache cleanup can produce the GMP leak-report pattern seen in the preserved unrestricted test run.
rug_library: Use the exact ASan-instrumented Rug rlib and dependency/native libraries from the closed normal-image-asan-v2 build; do not rebuild or modify that target.
difference: Both modes drop all Float values and join both workers. Both clear shared/main-thread caches after joining. Only cleanup calls rug::float::free_cache(FreeCache::Local) inside each worker before it exits.
output_contract: Both modes must produce byte-identical serialized values in joined-worker order. The retain mode must report a nonzero leak through GMP, without a scanner fatal error or invalid-access diagnostic; cleanup must exit zero without any sanitizer error.
execution_context: Prepare and review the binary first. Run the two native controls using exec_command require_escalated so LeakSanitizer can inspect threads. Leak detection stays enabled, with no inherited suppressions.
limits: This is a standalone cache-lifecycle control, not a new library qualification or a performance sample.
A positive result demonstrates this mechanism for two workers and three MPFR functions. It does not yet explain every allocation in the original 163672-byte report.
No Hyperreal production code is linked or changed. A test-harness cleanup fix still requires independent review and complete qualification.
